name: Zurgo and Ojutai
oracle_text:
Flying, haste
Zurgo and Ojutai has hexproof as long as it entered this turn.
Whenever one or more Dragons you control deal combat damage to a player or battle, look at the top three cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order. You may return one of those Dragons to its owner's hand.
blocked_sentences: Whenever one or more Dragons you control deal combat damage to a player or battle, look at the top three cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order. You may return one of those Dragons to its owner's hand.

needs.what: the `creatures_deal_combat_damage` event has to gain (a) a **filter over the connecting creatures** -- "one or more **Dragons** you control" -- and (b) a `damagers` list binding naming exactly those creatures, so the last clause can point `may` + `return_to_hand` at `{"binding": "damagers"}` with a `count: 1`. `_fire_damage_batch` already collects `batch["damagers"]` and puts it on the event; the two missing pieces are a per-event hook in `_matches` that keeps the firing only when at least one damager matches `spec.filter` (the subject-oid path cannot be reused, because the subject here is deliberately a player), and `"damagers"` added to `EVENT_BINDING_KEYS` beside `"attackers"`, which is the same list-of-oids shape `resolve_pool` already accepts.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `creatures_deal_combat_damage` is the only batched combat-damage event and is documented as having a **player** subject: it is deliberately absent from `OBJECT_SUBJECT_TRIGGERS`, so `_subject_oid` returns None and `_matches` short-circuits `if spec.filter is not None: if subject_oid is None: return False` -- a `filter: {"subtypes": ["Dragon"]}` on it makes the ability fire never, silently. Its payload `damagers` is not in `EVENT_BINDING_KEYS`, so "those Dragons" has no name to be reached by; `{"zone": "battlefield", "subtypes": ["Dragon"], "controller": "you"}` is the near miss and says something strictly larger -- every Dragon you control, including the ones that stayed home. `deals_combat_damage_to_player` is the other candidate and is per *connection*: it takes a filter but fires once per Dragon that got through, so a three-Dragon swing would look at nine cards and put three in hand, where the printed line is one firing however many connected. `batched: true` cannot repair it -- `_queue` keys the batch off `event.data["batch"]`, and neither `damage_player` nor `_fire_damage_batch` writes that key, so the guard is a no-op on every combat damage event.

needs.what: combat damage dealt **to a battle** -- battles as a permanent that can be attacked and damaged, and the resulting damage reflected in whatever trigger covers the sentence above, so "deal combat damage to a player or battle" fires on the battle half as well.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `Battle` exists in `types` and in `EnumPermanentType`, but nothing in `engine/combat.py` ever treats one as a thing that can be attacked: `attack_targets` offers players and planeswalkers only, `DamageAssignment` carries `to_player` / `to_object`, and `_fire_damage_batch` filters to assignments with `to_player is not None`. There is no `deals_combat_damage_to_battle` event, and `or_planeswalker` -- the one key in the vocabulary that widens an attack beyond a player -- names planeswalkers and nothing else. Writing the trigger for the player half alone would be the approximation: it is a strictly narrower card in any game with a battle on the board.

notes: The `entered_this_turn` need is RESOLVED and has been removed, with its printed sentence: "Zurgo and Ojutai has hexproof as long as it entered this turn" is now `{"kind": "static", "effect": "grant_keyword", "keywords": ["hexproof"], "affects": {"self_only": true, "entered_this_turn": true}}` -- a new key in STATIC_FILTER_KEYS answered from `TurnLedger.entered_this_turn(oid)`. Not the `self_only` clause on ENTERED_FILTER_KEYS this record asked for, and not `GameObject.entered_turn` either: `change_control` stamps that field for 302.6, so a filter reading it would hand a stolen commander hexproof. The two needs left are the batched combat-damage trigger and battles; the card stays unauthored until both land.
